newsitem.title: KENYA: Air controllers said arrested at Nairobi airport.
newsitem.headline: Air controllers said arrested at Nairobi airport.

text.p: Six air traffic controllers were said on Friday to have been arrested on Thursday afternoon after threatening to continue a go-slow at Nairobi airport only hours after their colleagues agreed to end a wage dispute with the government.
"Six air traffic controllers have been arrested late yesterday afternoon, and since then many controllers have not turned up out of fear of being arrested," said an air traffic controller.

He said he himself not had been arrested because he had not signed a letter with other air traffic controllers who had wanted to continue the go-slow and push their demands for better pay and working conditions.
On Thursday, the government announced an end to the five-day old dispute in which the controllers had demanded a 50-fold wage increase.

The air traffic controllers said they would return to normal working after being assured that a report on working conditions for government workers presented to President Daniel arap Moi on Wednesday would meet their concerns.

Police could not immediately be reached on Friday for confirmation of the arrests, but The Daily Nation newspaper reported that six controllers had been detained and kept overnight for questioning at a local police station.
Freight forwarders and foreign airlines said on Thursday afternoon they were facing only minor delays at Nairobi airport.
The airlines and freight forwarders could not be reached for comment on Friday as many had closed their offices because of a one-day national strike called by Kenya's opposition.
The centre of Nairobi was calm on Friday morning but most shops were closed in case of looting.
